chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaanah, who said:

I asked him about a man who rents land that has date palms or fruit trees for two or three years. He said: 'If he rents it when the fruit's sprouts become distinct and makes the contract, there is no harm. And if he rents it for two or three years, there is no harm in him renting it before it bears fruit.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for validly renting agricultural land with fruit trees in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of fixed-term land leases (muzara'ah) where the tenant rents land with existing palms or fruit trees for two or three years. It establishes that the contract is permissible whether concluded when the fruit is clearly visible (bayin) or before it bears fruit, emphasizing the flexibility in timing as long as the subject matter is defined. This ruling supports the Shia juristic principle of allowing agricultural partnerships with clear terms, distinguishing them from prohibited uncertainty (gharar).
